hero.headline: "Have you stopped cheating yet?" — and your child instantly starts defending themselves?
hero.subheadline: The accusation is already built into the question. Any answer sounds like an admission of guilt. This isn't a question — it's a trap.

media.alt: A child confused and cornered by a loaded trap question

pain.title: A loaded question: when any answer is a loss
pain.body:
"Have you stopped cheating yet?", "did you do it again?" — in class, in front of everyone, in conversation with adults. The child is stuck: say "yes" and they admit guilt; say "no" and it sounds just as bad. They start defending themselves or go silent.

This isn't a question — it's manipulation: a "fact" is already embedded in the question before the child has had a chance to check if it's true. To answer at all, they must accept the assumption. Without the skill to spot the trap, they defend instead of stopping the question itself.

The result — the child looks guilty even when they've done nothing. Others see the defensiveness and draw conclusions. And the child has no idea how it happened.

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 10–16 year olds. At this age, children are receptive to new thinking patterns and are still forming their views.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
